items.title: $CHPY The AI selloff is becoming increasingly disconnected from the underlying fundamentals. This selloff was triggered via the earnings rep
items.content_excerpt: $CHPY The AI selloff is becoming increasingly disconnected from the underlying fundamentals. This selloff was triggered via the earnings report from $GOOGL , despite continued growth in AI infrastructure demand and cloud computing. Short sellers are taking advantage of fragile sentiment. Earnings-related selling created the opening, and bearish positioning and momentum amplified the downside. This stock selloff does not mean that the AI growth cycle is over. $TSM and $NVDA remains positioned at the center of an infrastructure buildout that is still expanding. Hyperscaler AI spending isn’t disappearing because Wall Street temporarily gets nervous about returns. This is a valuation reset and a sentiment battle, not evidence that AI demand has collapsed. I still believe the recovery into 2027 remains the most likely outcome. The market is creating volatility, but the underlying AI opportunity hasn’t disappeared.

items.content_excerpt: $NVDA $CABA $PLUG $SIDU $QBTS rotation setup is getting harder to ignore. The Fed held rates—no hike—and big tech is finally showing cracks after leading the market for years. Meanwhile, the Russell 2000 gained 1% Thursday as the Nasdaq fell 1.4%, and small caps are leading this week. Now add the possibility of progress toward an Iran deal. If oil and inflation pressure ease, smaller, rate-sensitive companies could get a powerful tailwind. We saw how fast this can move in July 2024: the Russell 2000 surged roughly 11.5% in five sessions as money rotated out of mega-cap tech and into small caps. The market doesn’t wait for every headline to be confirmed. Smart money starts positioning when the odds begin to shift. I think we may be watching the early stages of that rotation now. Keep your eyes on the Russell.

items.content_excerpt: Microsoft announced a $25 billion bond offering to help finance its massive AI infrastructure expansion, taking advantage of its top-tier AAA credit rating and favorable access to debt markets. The offering is expected to close on November 4, with proceeds allocated to general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures, working capital, acquisitions, share repurchases and debt repayment. The company is targeting approximately $170 billion in capital expenditures for 2026 as it expands data centers and computing capacity to meet growing AI demand from customers including Anthropic and OpenAI. CFO Amy Hood said Microsoft plans to use external financing when market conditions are attractive, complementing its strong cash generation and existing leasing arrangements. Not long or short, just giving my opinion as a consumer.

items.content_excerpt: Microsoft announced a $25 billion bond offering to help finance its massive AI infrastructure expansion, taking advantage of its top-tier AAA credit rating and favorable access to debt markets. The offering is expected to close on November 4, with proceeds allocated to general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures, working capital, acquisitions, share repurchases and debt repayment. The company is targeting approximately $170 billion in capital expenditures for 2026 as it expands data centers and computing capacity to meet growing AI demand from customers including Anthropic and OpenAI. CFO Amy Hood said Microsoft plans to use external financing when market conditions are attractive, complementing its strong cash generation and existing leasing arrangements. Despite the significant borrowing, Microsoft reported positive free cash flow in its latest quarter, distinguishing itself from Alphabet, Meta and Amazon. $MSFT $AMZN $GOOGL $META

items.title: $CHPY The AI selloff is becoming increasingly disconnected from the underlying fundamentals. This selloff was triggered via the earnings rep
items.content_excerpt: $CHPY The AI selloff is becoming increasingly disconnected from the underlying fundamentals. This selloff was triggered via the earnings report from $GOOGL , despite continued growth in AI infrastructure demand and cloud computing. Short sellers are taking advantage of fragile sentiment. Earnings-related selling created the opening, and bearish positioning and momentum amplified the downside. This stock selloff does not mean that the AI growth cycle is over. $TSM and $NVDA remains positioned at the center of an infrastructure buildout that is still expanding. Hyperscaler AI spending isn’t disappearing because Wall Street temporarily gets nervous about returns. This is a valuation reset and a sentiment battle, not evidence that AI demand has collapsed. I still believe the recovery into 2027 remains the most likely outcome. The market is creating volatility, but the underlying AI opportunity hasn’t disappeared.

items.title: $RKLB BREAKING: SpaceX has reportedly told companies developing lunar landers for NASA that it will no longer provide launch services for th
items.content_excerpt: $RKLB BREAKING: SpaceX has reportedly told companies developing lunar landers for NASA that it will no longer provide launch services for their missions, according to new reporting by Ars Technica. The decision could complicate NASA's plans to establish a sustained presence on the Moon, as smaller lunar lander developers may need to turn to alternative rockets such as Blue Origin's New Glenn. The disclosure comes amid a broader shift in SpaceX's launch business: SpaceX $SPCX has told NASA it intends to retire Crew Dragon by 2030, reportedly stopped offering new commercial Falcon 9 launches beyond 2028, and declined to bid on three additional U.S. Space Force launch contracts. SpaceX continues to fulfill its existing government commitments, but the developments raise questions about NASA's growing dependence on a company increasingly focused on Starship, Starlink and AI infrastructure.

items.title: $IOVA I’m not sure why management chose to present such immature NSCLC data at this point when they could have waited another month or two a
items.content_excerpt: $IOVA I’m not sure why management chose to present such immature NSCLC data at this point when they could have waited another month or two and provided a more meaningful, mature dataset. Adding 30 new patients with substantially shorter follow-up was obviously going to pull down the overall mDOR and make durability appear shorter than it may ultimately prove to be. Vogt’s presentation was also unusually brief, confusing, and lacking in meaningful explanation. The overall tone seemed almost designed to invite a negative market reaction—exactly the opposite of the confidence and optimism he conveyed during the last earnings call. The bigger question is: why? Did management take advantage of the recent share-price strength, with the stock hovering around $14, to raise sufficient capital through the ATM? If they have already secured the funding they need, perhaps they are less concerned about supporting the share price in the near term. Any thoughts?

items.title: $IOVA HC Wainwright Our key takeaways from Iovance’s updated NSCLC data: Lifileucel demonstrated an approx. 25% ORR in mNSCLC; antitumor res
items.content_excerpt: $IOVA HC Wainwright Our key takeaways from Iovance’s updated NSCLC data: Lifileucel demonstrated an approx. 25% ORR in mNSCLC; antitumor response increased to approx. 59% in a retrospective analyses of study subgroups. After the opening, the stock is down approx. -32% (vs. +0.67% XBI). We think this is an overreaction likely based on modest response data in an entire patient population and/or perceived regulatory risks. We believe these results, in tandem with additional frontline NSCLC data, support subsequent registrational trials along with planned sBLA in 2027. IOV-LUN-202 update underscores TIL potential in NSCLC. This morning, Iovance announced a positive update to its Phase 2 IOV-LUN-202 trial investigating a one time lifileucel administration to patients with previously treated mNSCLC. This update disclosed results from 69 patients in Cohorts 1 and 2 whose disease had progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and ICI therapy.

items.content_excerpt: $IOVA Investors have focused on Iovance’s disappointing 8.5% response rate in patients outside its biomarker-enriched NSCLC subgroup, versus 59.1% in the enriched population. But the market may be overlooking an important opportunity: Iovance’s next-generation TIL pipeline, two programs of which could potentially address mechanisms underlying poor treatment response: * IOV-4001 (PD-1 Knockout TIL): Designed to overcome checkpoint-mediated immune suppression. * IOV-5001 (IL-12-Engineered TIL): Designed to enhance T-cell activity in challenging tumor microenvironments. If Iovance can establish conventional TIL for biomarker-enriched patients and engineered TIL for less-responsive patients, its long-term commercial opportunity could extend well beyond the currently identified high-response subgroup.

items.title: $IOVA Easy read Wells Fargo. Company Update — October 29, 2026 Biotechnology Iovance Biotherapeutics Updated 2L mNSCLC Data with Promising B
items.content_excerpt: $IOVA Easy read Wells Fargo. Company Update — October 29, 2026 Biotechnology Iovance Biotherapeutics Updated 2L mNSCLC Data with Promising Biomarker-Enrichment Strategy Our Call We note 59% ORR in KRAS WT/HER2 WT/ever-smokers strengthens TIL’s value proposition in 2L nsq-mNSCLC. Overall pop’s ORR held at 25%, mDOR was immature (~1 yr), and reduced LD led to improved safety, cutting Gr5 AE in half & cutting hosp. days >50%. We think today’s stock weakness could be due to concerns regarding durability and whether reduced lymphodepletion (LD) impacted DOR. We note if TIL expansion was impaired (from insufficient LD), ORR probably would have been impacted, which we note is not the case. We therefore expect mature DOR data to still be positive and clearing our experts’ bar of 12 months. With final data-cut expected in early ’27, we expect focus for the NSCLC program to rotate to FDA discussions and BLA filing.

items.content_excerpt: Starbucks is showing signs of a turnaround, as new beverages, store renovations and efforts to improve the customer experience help bring consumers back. The company beat expectations on a key comparable-sales metric, suggesting its recovery strategy is gaining traction. However, investors remain concerned that the improvement may not be happening quickly enough. For its fiscal year ending September 2027, Starbucks forecast an approximately 1% revenue decline, largely reflecting its decision to transfer its China retail operations to a joint venture. As a result, sales from those stores will no longer be included in the company's consolidated revenue, creating a headwind for reported growth despite potentially improving underlying business performance. The China restructuring is an important part of Starbucks' broader strategy to adapt to local competition and improve operations in one of its key international markets. $SBUX

Microsoft announced a $25 billion bond offering to help finance its massive AI infrastructure expansion, taking advantage of its top-tier AAA credit rating and favorable access to debt markets.
